prompt: Write a method that reverses the order of the words in a string. Complete the reverseWordOrder method in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Trimming and splitting on \\s+ turns any messy spacing into a clean array of words, which is why the output can always use single spaces no matter how the input looked. Walking the array from the last index down to 0 reverses the word order without reversing the letters inside each word. Appending the separator only between words (not after the last one) avoids a trailing space.
hints: trim() first, then split("\\s+") -- that handles extra spaces and gives you a clean String[] of words.
Loop the array backwards: for (int i = words.length - 1; i >= 0; i--).
Append a space only when another word still follows (i > 0), so the result has no trailing space.
